Select edges within one group by posterior probability

Source: R/edge_probs.R
select_edges.Rd

Selects the edges of one group's graph from the per-edge posterior probabilities of edge_probs(), either by the median-probability rule (probability > 0.5) or by Bayesian FDR control (bayes_fdr()).

Usage

select_edges(
  fit,
  group = 1,
  rule = c("structural", "magnitude", "cut", "median_shrinkage", "shrinkage", "interval"),
  c = NULL,
  decision = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  scale = c("precision", "pcor"),
  chain = NULL,
  level = 0.5
)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list.

group

The group whose graph to select. Default 1.

rule
"structural"

(default) \(P(G_{k,ij} = 1)\) (G-Wishart, SSVS) or \(P(w_{k,ij} > 0.5)\) (mGHS).

"magnitude"

\(P(|x_{k,ij}| > c)\) on scale.

"cut"

mGHS only: \(P(Z_{k,ij} = 1)\), the cut-model indicator.

"median_shrinkage"

mGHS only: the authors' median rule \(E[w_{k,ij}] > 0.5\). \(E[w]\) is not a probability, so only decision = "median" applies and no FDR is estimated.

"shrinkage"

mGHS only: \(E[1 - \kappa_{k,ij}]\), where \(\kappa\) is the edge's shrinkage factor in its column update with the global scale included: with \(a = \mu \tau_k \lambda^2_{ij,k} s_{jj} (\Omega_{-j}^{-1})_{ii}\) (prior variance times likelihood precision), \(1 - \kappa = a / (1 + a)\), averaged over the two column updates of the edge and over iterations. In horseshoe regression \(1 - \kappa\) is read as a pseudo inclusion probability (Carvalho, Polson & Scott 2010). It measures how much the data dominate the prior for the edge, not whether the edge is nonzero, so it grows with \(n\) for null edges too. With correlated groups an edge is shrunk towards the value the other groups predict, and the approximation ignores coupling between edges. decision = "median" (\(E[1 - \kappa] > 0.5\)) is the default; "bfdr" treats it as a probability. In simulations (p = 8 and 20, n = 100 to 1000) it ranked edges as well as \(E[w]\), but neither 0.5 rule controlled false edges: at p = 20, n = 100, \(E[1 - \kappa] > 0.5\) selected 3 null edges against 65 for \(E[w] > 0.5\); at p = 8, n = 300, 17 against 0. For selection with error control use rule = "magnitude".

"interval"

The central credible interval at level level excludes zero, i.e. p_sign \(> (1 + \) level\() / 2\). With level = 0.5 this is the graphical horseshoe's published rule (Li, Craig & Bhadra 2019). It is a sign rule: as \(n\) grows it selects null edges whose small estimates are well determined, so it is offered for comparison, with no FDR estimate.

c

Threshold for rule = "magnitude".

decision

"bfdr" (default; "median" for rule = "median_shrinkage" and "shrinkage") selects the largest set with posterior expected FDR at most alpha, keeping tied probabilities together; "median" selects probability > 0.5.

alpha

Target posterior expected FDR for decision = "bfdr".

scale

"precision" (default) or "pcor": the scale of mean, sd, p_exceed_*, p_union_* and p_sign.

chain

NULL (default) pools all chains; an integer selects chains.

level

Credible level for rule = "interval" (default 0.5).

Value

An object of class "multiggm_edge_selection": a list with selected (logical p x p), prob, edges (the selected edges with their probability and Bayesian FDR q-value, see bfdr_qvalues()), expected_fdr (posterior expected FDR of the selected set), n_selected, alpha, rule, c, decision, scale and group.

See also

edge_probs(), select_diff_edges(), bayes_fdr()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                     burnin = 100, nsave = 100, save_draws = FALSE)
select_edges(fit, group = 1, decision = "median")
#> <multiggm_edge_selection>
#>   Group 1, rule: structural, decision: median
#>   Selected 4 edges with value > 0.5 (posterior expected FDR 0.175)
#>   i j prob    q_value
#> 1 5 6 1.00 0.00000000
#> 2 2 3 0.92 0.04000000
#> 3 4 5 0.80 0.09333333
#> 4 1 3 0.58 0.17500000
